summary: Bugbear's physics-heavy demolition racing series and its later Team6/Kylotonn sequels, focused on crash damage, ragdoll stunt events, and destructive arcade races.

entries.title: FlatOut

emulation.notes: Console emulation is optional for preservation or local-multiplayer nostalgia, but the PC release is the main route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC resolution/settings plus Workshop support

primary.why: The original FlatOut shipped on Windows, PlayStation 2, and Xbox. The modern PC release now has the best fidelity ceiling plus a 2024 update with Steam Workshop, Steam Deck support, and quality-of-life improvements, while the console versions are lower-resolution routes with no sourced exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Steam/Windows release; use the 2024 update, high resolution, controller support, and Workshop fixes/mods where desired.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release; modern Steam build received Workshop, Steam Deck, and quality-of-life updates in 2024.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity ceiling and the maintained modern release.

all_releases.fidelity: Lower-resolution console version with two-player split-screen.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over PC and lower fidelity.

all_releases.fidelity: Console version with four-player split-screen and System Link.
all_releases.reason: skip: local multiplayer features are notable, but no unique career/content advantage over PC for the main archive route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Windows release is both the best-fidelity route and the complete main version; console local multiplayer differences are not required for a single-player complete playthrough.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; the current PC build is an updated original release rather than a remake.

entries.title: FlatOut 2

emulation.notes: Console versions can be emulated for preservation, but PC is preferred.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC resolution/settings plus Workshop support

primary.why: FlatOut 2 launched on Windows, PlayStation 2, and Xbox, later receiving an OS X port. The current PC release has the best fidelity ceiling and received a 2024 update adding Workshop, Steam Deck support, and quality-of-life fixes. Ultimate Carnage is treated separately because it is an enhanced version with different content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the updated Windows/Steam release at high resolution; use Workshop/modern compatibility support from the 2024 update where desired.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release; modern Steam build received Workshop, Steam Deck, and quality-of-life updates in 2024.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity ceiling and current maintained route.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over PC.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over PC.
skip: useful alternate PC-family port, but no sourced content advantage over the updated Windows release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: For FlatOut 2 specifically, the Windows release is the best-fidelity and complete route; Ultimate Carnage's enhanced content is a separate archive entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ultimate Carnage is not a patch over FlatOut 2; it is an enhanced separate release with its own entry.

entries.title: FlatOut: Ultimate Carnage
entries.definitive_edition: FlatOut: Ultimate Carnage Collector's Edition on Windows

emulation.notes: Xbox 360 emulation is optional, but the PC release is the recommended main route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC resolution/settings plus Workshop support

primary.why: Ultimate Carnage is the enhanced FlatOut 2 release with improved graphics, Carnage mode, more on-track opponents, and extra content. The Windows version has the best fidelity ceiling and received the same 2024 Workshop/Steam Deck/quality-of-life update as the earlier PC games.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows/Steam Collector's Edition; use high resolution and modern compatibility settings, with Workshop support where useful.

all_releases.fidelity: Original HD console release of the enhanced FlatOut 2 package.
all_releases.reason: skip: historically important and complete, but lower fidelity ceiling than PC.

all_releases.fidelity: PC version of the enhanced release; modern Steam build received Workshop, Steam Deck, and quality-of-life updates in 2024.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity route for Ultimate Carnage and complete enhanced content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Windows release carries the enhanced content and highest fidelity ceiling.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is an enhanced remake/reworking of FlatOut 2 rather than a replacement for every FlatOut 2 detail; keep both entries distinct.

entries.title: FlatOut: Head On

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP internal resolution scaling for cleaner output while preserving the PSP version.

primary.why: Head On is the PSP adaptation of the Ultimate Carnage branch and was released only for PlayStation Portable. It is the sole sourced version, so PSP/PPSSPP is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release on original hardware or PPSSPP with internal resolution scaling.

all_releases.fidelity: Only release, portable adaptation of the Ultimate Carnage content line.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or modern official port is sourced.

entries.title: FlatOut (Wii)

emulation.notes: Use original hardware if emulator compatibility is imperfect; Dolphin can raise internal resolution when compatible.

primary.why: The 2010 Wii FlatOut is a distinct Team6-developed Wii entry rather than the Bugbear original. Wii is the only sourced platform, so it is the required version despite being lower fidelity than the earlier PC games.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Wii/Wii U hardware or Dolphin with standard compatibility testing.

all_releases.fidelity: Only release of the Team6-developed Wii entry.
all_releases.reason: primary: sole sourced platform and complete version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only Wii is sourced for this distinct entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or modern port is sourced.

entries.title: FlatOut 3: Chaos & Destruction

primary.why: FlatOut 3 was released exclusively for Microsoft Windows. It is therefore both the highest-fidelity and complete version, even though its reception was notably poor.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/Steam release on a modern PC compatibility setup.

all_releases.reason: primary: sole platform and complete version.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or alternate platform release is sourced.

entries.title: FlatOut Stuntman

primary.why: FlatOut Stuntman is sourced as an Android-exclusive ragdoll/stunt spin-off developed and published by Team6. Android is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved Android installation on compatible hardware or an Android preservation/emulation setup; expect delisting risk.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release, mobile ragdoll stunt spin-off.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile delisting/preservation may make legal access difficult.
